**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep background jobs stopped during the canary**

When the documented production `serve` profile is started with provider credentials for the canary, these overrides stop only discovery and reputation jobs. API boot unconditionally starts the records, Instagram, social-auto-reply, campaign, operations, provider-event, and reservation workers (`tdf-hq/src/TDF/App/Boot.hs` lines 162-172), and the social loop processes work immediately rather than waiting for a daily slot. This can mutate the restored database or send provider messages before validation and before writes are reopened; add a global canary/worker-disable gate or run the canary with credentials and permissions that prevent every background worker.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Run the owned-URL rewrite during final restore**

The final cutover sequence never invokes the newly added `migrate-owned-urls.sql`—a repository-wide search finds it mentioned only in the rehearsal evidence, and it is intentionally absent from the production migration manifest. Following this runbook therefore leaves stored asset, event-image, and radio URLs on `tdf-hq.fly.dev`; once the superseded Fly service is retired as instructed, those existing images and streams break. Add the script and its idempotence/projection checks to the fenced final-restore steps.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Build verification SQL from the requested revision**

When this command is run from a checkout whose HEAD differs from the supplied release SHA, the migrations and emergency preflight come from that SHA, but `preflight.sql` and `verify.sql` are generated by the currently checked-out `scripts/lib/production-release.mjs`. The resulting bundle can therefore validate a different schema contract than the reviewed image while `release.json` still labels it with the requested SHA. Require the tooling checkout to match the target revision or load/version these builders from that revision before emitting the artifact.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Honor the runtime API-base override for asset URLs**

In deployments that supply `VITE_API_BASE` through the supported `window.__ENV__` runtime configuration rather than baking it with Vite, normal API calls honor that value through `resolveApiBase()`, but this constant ignores it and now falls back to `api.tdfrecords.net`. Relative inventory photos are consequently fetched from a different backend; the duplicated constant in `MarketplacePage.tsx` has the same problem. Use the shared resolver so runtime-configured deployments keep API and asset hosts aligned.
